reviews.text: At time of writing this there are no other reviews. WHich is a shame because honestly this game is pretty legit. It's a roguelike and some people don't like those. I'm one of those people. I hate roguelike games. Yet I found myself really enjoying this one and really wanting to play it. The game has kickass music, it has a fun reptetive gameplay mechanic. It's interesting, it's got great progression considering what type of game it is. And overall it was just a lot of fun to play. It never broke or glitched out on me, it's got a decent price, it's gonna have a long playtime and considering it's in early access it never once felt like it was early access. Maybe it's just content thats missing? I don't know. But I was having fun with it and I normally hate these games so that's gotta be a good sign. I'd highly encourage everyone to check out this game, even if your not normally a fan of roguelikes. But if you'd like some more information with some legit gameplay then please check out the video on my YouTube Channel (link below). Otherwise thanks so much for reading and I hope I managed to help some of you out there to spend your money wisely. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_9ZW-qqWMPQ

For now I played under 2 hours (will update the review if I have anything to add or change), but so far I can say - this mix of FTL-like progression and Darkest Dungeon-esque combat actually works. I tried playing some other games that have this style of combat but I couldn't stick - here it's nice though. The music also fits nicely. The game says to focus on storybuilding and I can see that. I do worry though that the story will quickly become repetitive/generic much like in FTL. That said, this game just released to Early Access, so let's see how far they'll push it. All in all, it is fun, even though I usually don't like games with this combat style too much. Well done, I can recommend!

updating review cos i've played more (it's fun) It's a roguelike with unlockable characters/abilities, an interesting/unusual setting and interesting mechanics/options already implemented initial combat can be quite difficult and I'm pretty sure there's no expectation you beat the game on the first playthrough, so it can feel oppressive at first. Once you have experience with a few characters and understand how to use buffs/debuffs effectively you can do a lot, in a lot of different ways, which is a good sign really looking forward to coming back and trying new stuff as this game is expanded and interest picks up

Great little game so far. Excited to see where it goes but for now the game play and direction of the story feel really good! The music is incredible and I enjoyed listening to the different songs for the different areas. Combat was tough! I found my self dying often and not getting very far, but that's probably cause I don't play these kind of games very often. The game reminds me of sly the spire but with the deck. instead the randomness comes from the survivors you meet along the way. Each survivor plays differently and you can unlock them the more you find them throughout your runs. This loop had me putting several runs back to back to see who else I'd bump into during my zombie slaying adventure. For the price this game delivers even now. I wouldn't hesitate to pick this one up and enjoy it even in early access.

So this game definitely delivers on being a rogue-like and each run is *ahem* almost not the same experience. I love zombie games and love rogue likes ranging from FTL to Slay The Spire. I would say there are some definite pros and cons to this game. Pros: Not very expensive for the possibility of entertainment you will get out of it, even for being early access. Good selection of characters with a wide array of unique abilities. A character unlocking and ability unlocking progression system that allows you more access to characters abilities and other characters from the start of the game the more you play, very interesting system. Cons: The game currently seems a bit unbalanced in terms of enemy difficulty. The beginning enemies can seem to be absolute pushovers at first and as soon as your party gets filled up to 4 characters in the second "area" you will start encountering enemies that, if you happen to have a sub-balanced party with a good spread of damage and protection skills you will 9 times out of 10 get the floor mopped with your whole party. Speaking of unbalanced, I don't know if this is just me but the usefulness of character skills compared to the length of time you have to wait before that character makes another move seems to be far too long, for every two skills or attacks my characters played out it seemed like the enemies got double the amount of attacks and thus, double the amount of damage output as my own party, especially the hound enemies and the frantic undead seem to have very quick attacks and easily outpace almost any characters I've unlocked thus far. you should always have a chance to get to the end of the game and not have to bash your head against an undead wall for upwards of two and a half to 3 hours with 15 different runs all ending in TPK's in 1 single fight; Not kidding, I had six characters and they ALL died in 1 skirmish in a non-boss fight. Anyways, the game is good but can be frustrating at times. it definitely needs some tweaking with enemy skills and delays in skill usage. Nominally, a slight buff to some if not more character skills so the delay does not force you to watch each enemy bite on your team for 2-3 attacks each before your own team even gets to start going again. A solid 6.5 out of 10 Edit: one other con would be have a small selection of bosses per area. Instead of the same 1 boss for each zone make it a 1 in 2 or 1 in 3 choice, to encourage people to not try to build specifically to counter the one known boss.

Put in a couple hours and a few runs to get something of an idea together about this game. It really gives me the old school Armor Games vibes (i.e. Sonny) with its pixel art and Turn-based JRPG combat system. It is a pretty punishing game and while its combat system feels a little unfair (if your luck is kinda meh and your team comp isn't cohesive) at first, as I started to understand the mechanics it got a little "easier". You do a little better each run, and as you do more runs your survivors level up giving you access to their better abilities at the start. The encounters on the map are kind of samey however (in my limited playtime anyways. Your mileage may vary), but with more development that could be easily solved. I'm usually not a big fan of the roguelike genre (and I'm still not with this game in my library), but it does have a certain nostalgic charm to it that I kind of dig. If this type of game is your bread and butter, I'd recommend you give it a shot as it is fairly cheap. It seems to have a good amount of room to grow, and is already pretty solid.
Good stuff. Can't wait to see where it goes.

Incredibly solid turn-based combat with a heavy focus on manipulating the turn-order timeline to your advantage, with fantastic pixel art and a jamming soundtrack. My only beef is that the runs take waaaaaaaay too long. Like, 2 hours minimum, if not moreso. Definitely could use some more character ability customization too.

This game is fun. Enjoy the brutal tactics. Some of the characters are rough around the edges and are currently under the knife for reworking some of them. However its fun to try out characters and get to see what makes them work. Having only the selection of two characters to start with certainly assures you of playing with new characters you haven't seen before each time. I have a youtube channel Troy Tactical Gaming and i've been live streaming the game. Check it out! Enjoy!

This is a solid, rogue-like game. Each playthrough takes about 2 hours (3 maps). It can be difficult but you'll catch on to the combinations of tactics based on the team members you find. This is definitely a game about managing and exploiting stats, but it's fairly simple to figure out. Honestly, it's a good way to kill some time. It sucks you in but when you finish a playthrough, you're done for the day. It has a good formula. Devs are also quick to respond in the forums and they listen to complaints and suggestions. I don't know why this game is not more popular than it is but maybe it will pick up over time.

I've been playing this since before EA, and it's been solid and fun for quite a while now, but last few updates certainly add a lot more content and overall polish. Certainly not a game for everyone, so be warned: there is a lot of chance and a lot of synergies involved. So at first you might often end up in seemingly unwinnable scenarios, or sometimes might accidentally get OP and plow through the whole run without a scratch. But worry not: as you learn character traits and various mechanics, you'll learn to avoid those unwinnable battles (most of the time!). And when you finally feel the need for more pain and suffering, the game has a bunch of additional challenge modes to help you, the cruelest one for sure being monsters gaining a pretty strong regen (which your characters don't have at all, in case you wondered). I do think a less random daily/weekly challenge mode would be a great addition. But at least now we got all these fresh cheevos to put in a few more hours for :) Also can confirm Riga really looks like that even without the zombies, although I'm not entirely sure about some of my neighbors. The TV tower still stands though.

This game is.. fine. It really only has the turn-based combat going for it. For a game set in a zombie apocalypse, it really doesn't make you feel any urgency or dread. The setting itself is basically a non-factor. It could be anything else and it wouldn't make any difference. It doesn't do a good job introducing you to the world and the game itself, so I feel no attachment to the characters. I'm not even sure what their objective is. I didn't read any of the story because the game didn't interest me to want to read it. I don't feel any motivation to see the characters survive each fight. I feel no difference whether I win or lose, so why even play the game? The turn-based combat could still be pretty fun, so I could see people getting behind this game. But there's a bunch of other turn-based games that also has a great combat while having a great narrative/setting. Games that actually make you want to play them.
As general steam deck grievous once said: Ah a fine addition to my collection

A great game for fans of turn-based roguelike RPGs with great pixelart and good music. The initial learning curve may be steep as you don't get much information on the different game mechanics in the beginning, but none of them are overly complicated so you will soon get the hang of it. However, don't get me wrong - even a veteran player can still encounter very challenging situations. Overall, “Stories from the Outbreak” is a fun and challenging game that’s worth checking out if you enjoy the zombie theme and turn-based RPGs.

TLDR - turn-based roguelike in an oddly charming pixel art zombie apocalypse. I think the game itself is pretty decent, my lack of recommendation comes down to personal taste. In short, peeling back all the parts I didn't find enjoyable leaves a game that doesn't deliver on price. Overall I think the game is decently done, pixel art looks great and the setting is interesting. I enjoyed reading randomly discovered notes to uncover lore about the world, about other survivors, about what life was before the apocalyptic event. Combat is interesting although sometimes I would fail encounters because a new enemy/mechanic appeared that I hadn't seen before and was not prepared to deal with. Further gripes listed below in no particular order: - discovering the optimal ways to resolve random events was pretty tedious given the length of runs and node rng: especially disliked 'evil' choices being punished in one type of event but not another, sucks to be handicapped by an event because you had no way of knowing the outcome - inspiration (ability/stat points) is hard to come by, it's a pain that choosing an ability upgrade costs twice as much as gambling a random ability upgrade. - training is often necessary to get enough inspiration over the course of a run but it's not very enjoyable to interact with: you either have to handle encounters short a character or recruit additional characters that will cost you more food/fuel - can often feel pretty anaemic by the time you reach the final boss if you got unlucky with events, characters, opportunities to train etc - none of which are truly in your control - personally I've always hated 'mirror/copycat/theft' mechanics being used by the enemy ie. character's next attack does the same damage to themselves, any healing/protection this character gains is given to the entire enemy team, steal buffs from your character and give them to an enemy. Working up through the challenges felt unfun (not impossible just not enjoyable). Glass bead (capping max protection to 25/100) is pretty brutal since you need protection to deal with all the incoming damage from the rest of the modifiers. It also neuters characters designed to stack protection. Between Black Bag and Broken Mirror I was less excited about discovering new trinkets and more dreading how they might interact when given to enemies, or which trinkets I could write off as fodder to sacrifice. I know they're challenge modifiers but it's just not fun to get all these new toys but be forced to lose them or have them given to the enemy.

Relatively short game. Theoretically a game you could replay several times but its highly frustrating. Sometimes you get enemy zombies which are just to strong and wipe your team. And there are near to no possabilities to heal your team except the weird ones where you can hope that you have enough apples, otherwise you get ♥♥♥♥♥♥ even harder because you dont have enough apples. Theoreically a funny casual game idea, but terribly balanced and voice over instead of text only would have been good for the game for the atmosphere..

Honestly, it comes across as a bit barebones for a game that, even on sale, I feel is a bit overpriced. I wanted to give it a try since I love zombies and I love turn-based combat, but nothing in the writing nor gameplay strikes me as particularly interesting. If the price was lowered substantially, I could see myself giving this a more fair go, but at 20 bucks (15 on sale when I tried it) I feel like the minimal amount of content and depth I experienced in the first couple hours just didn't make it worthwhile. The UI was a little finicky and wouldn't respond to my clicks pretty frequently, and some of the writing comes across as a bit amateurish (I mean this in the nicest way I can, since this is clearly a small team effort). Again, maybe for an incredibly deep sale (as in maybe 5-8 bucks) I would repurchase the game and give it another go, but from what I've seen, I don't think it's quite worth the purchase.

Nice mix of initiative based combat with FTL style exploration with zombie infested Latvian cities in background. Pros: * Combat system gives you a lot of choices and party composition + trinkets allows you to explore different builds. * Art and music in this game captures Rīga in spirit and map is recognizable for anyone who lived in that city. * Story is nice if you're in a mood to read. Additional points for individual character stories in the end. Cons: * UI can take a bit of work, clicks sometimes didn't register the first time I clicked and it looks underpolished. * Freezed couple of times when I switched to a different desktop (macos)

Its OK. I think its overpriced. Even on sale for $12.99 on steam summer sale ( Canadian ) its a bit much. I played for almost 2 hours and did several runs, and I kinda just felt like I experienced most of what it has to offer. If it was like $5 or $10 regular priced, I would be fine recommending it. But at $26 CAD normal price? Thats just way too much for what you get here. Its very basic, though it is a decent game overall, the roguelike part works well and is fun, if a little repetitive due to how similar runs can be. The idea of a turn based, zombie RPG is a very cool one, the game is just a bit barebones for the asking price,
Good writing, overall a good game. A little overpriced, get it on sale. I didn't wanted to replay it, but for some, it surely would be a nice experience. Overall, 6/10.

Alright. [i]Stories from the Outbreak[/i] is done and dusted. At least inasmuch as I've finished the game with, I think eight(?) of the characters so far. Outright, I'll just say that this is a pretty fun little game that you can complete quickly, but in order to finish everything, you'll probably need to complete five to ten runs while also having the game play out completely in your favor for at least a couple of those. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3623179866 This is a node-based exploration game, you'll select node strands to follow as you work your way through each level. The third level is the final boss and ending level. The first level, you'll do a lot of levelling up, collecting party members and such, and as you progress, the game progressively also gets far more difficult. As you play through the second level, you will really need to have your party strategies dialed in. But even then, some bad enemy or random encounter nodes can end your run super quick. Everything is randomized to an extent, so luck is a true factor in having a successful run and getting at least a couple of your party members out of the city. So your goal, outside of collecting survivors to add to your party, is to gather enough food to rest and heal up between levels, gather enough gasoline to pay your way onto the ship that will take you away from the zombie outbreak, find trinkets that act as permanent buffs, and simply level up your characters in general. You earn inspiration points, which is this game's xp, and you will spend those either upgrading your stats or upgrading your abilities. Personally, I'd advise doing both, but starting with at least one ability upgrade. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3623179982 In order to accomplish all this, you will need to choose node paths that give you the best ability to land on food/gas/survivor/healing nodes, but you will also need to try to fight as often as possible to get the potential rewards from said fights. And random event nodes also can provide nice boosts to everything you need. But enemy nodes can sometimes generate enemies that exceed your party's skill and random events can turn south quickly depending on what you draw. When those things happen, it's generally at or close to the point where your party gets wiped. At the end of each level is a house you can rest at (assuming you have enough food) and then, rested or not, you get a boss battle before starting the next level. Funny thing is, I think the boss battle you get before actually getting to the boat is the easiest one. The ones you get in the first two levels ca be and are pretty brutal. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3623179808 Combat is turn based JRPG style with numbered sliders to indicate who goes next. Some abilities can be used to impact this slider, speeding up your turn and slowing down your enemy's, for example. Also, you build power in combat as you act, which will in turn give you special boosts or buffs, such as boosting shield and health, doing more damage, etc... It's worth noting that all the enemies have the same things available to them. So, they also earn boosts, buffs, and so on in combat. Combat stats are health and shield, but there are also timed effects such as bleeding and poison. It's a pretty effective system even though you will at times wish the enemies didn't receive the same considerations, lol. Graphics are pretty chill and yet appropriately evocative as well. Checking out the slides on the product page will give you a good sense for what's happening graphically. I think they look cool. The OST and other in-game sounds are nicely done as well and certainly continue with the theme offered with the graphics and setting. Where this game sees its main issue is in the randomly generated encounters. There are a fairly limited number of enemy types, and boss battles tend to repeat from run to run despite there being a greater variety. I don't know if something triggers widening the selection, but if it does, it takes its time doing so, lol. And I think it happens too often where bad luck node draws can ruin a run. What I would say in summation is that if you enjoy luck-affected turn-based zombie node exploration games, this is definitely that, and it does what it does pretty well, with a couple issues mentioned above. It's currently on sale for $7.99 at the time of this writing. That is a great price for this game, and you should have no problem getting your money's worth there. IDK that I'd want to spend the base $19.99 on it though. So, grab it on sale would be my advice. Stories from the Outbreak is a turn-based roguelike RPG developed and published by Coldwild Games that places a strong emphasis on tactical decision-making, emergent storytelling, and the psychological weight of survival in a collapsing world. Set during the early days of a devastating viral outbreak, the game frames its journey around a desperate attempt to escape a quarantined city before the final chance at evacuation disappears. Rather than presenting the apocalypse as a spectacle-driven power fantasy, it grounds the experience in uncertainty, scarcity, and human fragility, immediately establishing a somber tone that defines the entire adventure. At the core of the experience is a methodical turn-based combat system that rewards careful planning over reckless aggression. Battles are structured around positioning, ability synergy, and the distinct strengths and weaknesses of each survivor, making party composition a crucial element of success. Enemies are varied and often dangerous in unexpected ways, forcing players to constantly reassess tactics instead of relying on a single dominant strategy. The roguelike structure ensures that combat encounters remain tense, as mistakes can quickly spiral into irreversible losses, reinforcing the idea that survival is never guaranteed and that every encounter carries real risk. Between battles, the game leans heavily into exploration and narrative events, presented through a branching map filled with unpredictable encounters. These moments often take the form of text-driven scenarios that ask players to make difficult choices under pressure, such as whether to risk scarce resources for potential rewards or prioritize the safety and morale of the group. The writing gives these decisions real weight, frequently offering no clearly “correct” answer and instead reflecting the messy, morally ambiguous nature of survival in a broken society. Over time, these choices accumulate, shaping the overall tone of each run and making every journey feel personal and reactive to the player’s decisions. Character development is another standout aspect, as survivors are not interchangeable units but individuals with distinct personalities, backgrounds, and emotional states. As the journey unfolds, relationships can strengthen or fracture depending on how situations are handled, and the loss of a party member is felt both mechanically and narratively. This focus on character-driven storytelling elevates the game beyond a purely systems-based roguelike, transforming it into a series of interconnected human stories that explore fear, desperation, and fleeting hope. Even repeated playthroughs manage to feel fresh thanks to new combinations of survivors, events, and outcomes that subtly reshape the narrative each time. Visually, the pixel art presentation is understated but effective, using restrained color palettes and simple animations to convey mood rather than spectacle. The environments communicate decay and abandonment without excessive detail, allowing the player’s imagination to fill in the gaps. This minimalist approach pairs well with the audio design, where subdued music and ambient sounds reinforce the sense of isolation and tension without overwhelming the gameplay. While the visuals are not flashy, they are cohesive and purposeful, supporting the game’s thematic focus on bleak realism and emotional weight. In terms of replay value, the game offers a satisfying loop built around gradual mastery and long-term progression. Permanent unlocks and newly discovered story paths encourage repeated runs, while the inherent unpredictability of the roguelike structure ensures that no two attempts unfold in exactly the same way. Difficulty can be punishing, especially for newcomers, but the challenge feels intentional rather than unfair, reinforcing the harsh realities of the setting. Each failure becomes a lesson, pushing players to refine strategies and approach future runs with greater caution and foresight. Taken as a whole, Stories from the Outbreak is a thoughtful and emotionally grounded take on the zombie survival genre, one that prioritizes meaningful choices, character-driven storytelling, and strategic depth over spectacle. It excels at making players feel the consequences of their decisions, both in combat and in narrative moments, creating an experience that lingers long after a run ends. For fans of turn-based RPGs and roguelikes who appreciate strong writing and a somber, reflective tone, it stands as a compelling and memorable journey through the quiet horrors of societal collapse. Rating: 7/10

Fully released game from 2024; (last update was ; 19/7/24 Ver.1.1.2) It feels clunky, the UI is a bit all over the place, same thing as the enemy selection in battle, sometimes using the icon that appears on the top of the avalible target works, sometimes doesn't, the dialogue options are the same, sometimes you really need to click in the middle of the button for it to register. The battle system is akin to the one present on the Battle Chasers series, a timeline with a initiative bar that shows the turns and intentions of the enemies and your characters. There are no other language options apart from English. It has it's good things, the fact that you can cheese the whole game with a little planning and having the Doctor character (The one that gives CheatDeath to the whole team) + the poison centered character that can deal damage through armor is funny and makes the last boss a waiting game of managing Bleed/Poison and mantaining CD. There are a lot of synergies between characters, items and the events and lore have flavour. Its a challenging game that feels barebones, not worth the 20€ at all but would recommend at a price point around 7-12€ as far a replayability goes, it's a roguelike with teambuilding, I mean, you can play as much as you want but after 3.5h (3 runs, 2W-1L) I didn't feel compelled to keep playing.

After having finished two playthroughs (out of three), I don't really feel any itch to continue playing. There's no progression that does anything for me. Going back for another run of more of the same isn't really calling out to me. I'm not saying it's a bad game. I actually like it. I just… don't really want to play it? Would probably be fire as a board game with a couple of friends.

I've been playing since early access and I fell in love with this latvian zombie turn-based rougelike rpg from the first demo I played <3 I'm a bit of an addict, but I believe the game's rougelike loops are what keep me coming back, because the different synergies between characters make each run feel very distinct One thing that i don't particularly like is the asking price, which makes me not recommend as often as I do, however definitely get it on sale! I highly recommend it!! (Paldies par burvīgo spēli <3)
hidden gem of a game

game is a lot of fun its actually criminal how few people have played it. i rate it quite highly. its not as rougelite as youd expect more of randomised series of set events and locations in a semi random order. wish the leveling up was a little easier. never in any games have i ever gotten 4 inspiration points.

What an amazing hidden gem of a game! Nice pixel art, nice atmosphere, nice mechanics. Straight forward on the surface but with a lot of synergies that can absolutely break the game but you really feel clever when you pull it off. The best thing about this is how well designed are these synergies between the characters. But it has some good writing as well, surprisingly for the genre and the scope of the game which is not very big. I have beaten this three times before losing, but I overthink every turn. I think bad reviews about difficulty are just skill issue players that do not read. If you are doubting just get it, good times.
[DEMO] Far as zombie apocalypse roguelikes go, this is as terrific as they engineer. Infancy & balance issues aside; it ain't BAT at all! Maybe you've heard stories- well, all true. Good ones anyhow~
